- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward more aggressively.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; increase forecast slightly for such periods.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33–0.67), model exhibits lag; shift forecast slightly ahead of true trend to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the final 5–7 days; apply a “tail correction” by aligning last 3–5 forecast points with true outcome’s last 3–5 values.
